**Notation.** We interpret $\phi^5(q)_\infty := [\phi(q)]^5 = \left[\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)\right]^5$ and $\phi(q^5)_\infty := \phi(q^5) = \prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^{5n})$, where $q=e^{2\pi i\tau}$, $\operatorname{Im}\tau>0$. The limit $q\to1^-$ corresponds to $\tau\to0$ through the upper half-plane; write $\tau=it$, $t\to0^+$.

**Step 1 — Reduce to the Dedekind eta function.** Recall $\eta(\tau)=q^{1/24}\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)=q^{1/24}\phi(q)$, so $\phi(q)=q^{-1/24}\eta(\tau)$. Hence
$$
[\phi(q)]^5 = q^{-5/24}\eta(\tau)^5.
$$
For $\phi(q^5)$: since $q^5=e^{2\pi i(5\tau)}$,
$$
\phi(q^5)=(q^5)^{-1/24}\eta(5\tau)=q^{-5/24}\eta(5\tau).
$$
The powers $q^{-5/24}$ cancel, giving the exact identity
$$
\frac{[\phi(q)]^5}{\phi(q^5)}=\frac{\eta(\tau)^5}{\eta(5\tau)}. \tag{1}
$$

**Step 2 — Apply the modular transformation.** The Dedekind eta function satisfies
$$
\eta\!\left(-\frac{1}{\tau}\right)=\sqrt{-i\tau}\,\eta(\tau).
$$
Setting $\tau=it$ (so $-1/\tau=i/t$) yields $\eta(i/t)=\sqrt{t}\,\eta(it)$, i.e.
$$
\eta(it)=t^{-1/2}\eta(i/t),\qquad \eta(5it)=(5t)^{-1/2}\eta\!\bigl(i/(5t)\bigr).
$$
Substituting into (1):
$$
\frac{\eta(it)^5}{\eta(5it)}
=\frac{t^{-5/2}\,\eta(i/t)^5}{(5t)^{-1/2}\,\eta(i/(5t))}
=\sqrt{5}\,t^{-2}\,\frac{\eta(i/t)^5}{\eta(i/(5t))}. \tag{2}
$$

**Step 3 — Asymptotics of $\eta$ at the cusp.** For $y\to+\infty$,
$$
\eta(iy)=e^{-\pi y/12}\prod_{n\ge1}(1-e^{-2\pi ny})\sim e^{-\pi y/12},
$$
since the product $\to1$. Applying this with $y=1/t$ and $y=1/(5t)$ (both $\to\infty$ as $t\to0^+$):
$$
\eta(i/t)^5\sim e^{-5\pi/(12t)},\qquad \eta(i/(5t))\sim e^{-\pi/(60t)}.
$$
Therefore
$$
\frac{\eta(i/t)^5}{\eta(i/(5t))}\sim \exp\!\left(-\frac{5\pi}{12t}+\frac{\pi}{60t}\right)=\exp\!\left(-\frac{25\pi-\pi}{60t}\right)=\exp\!\left(-\frac{2\pi}{5t}\right). \tag{3}
$$

**Step 4 — Take the limit.** Combining (2) and (3),
$$
\frac{[\phi(q)]^5}{\phi(q^5)}\sim \sqrt{5}\,t^{-2}\,\exp\!\left(-\frac{2\pi}{5t}\right),\qquad t\to0^+.
$$
The exponential decay $e^{-2\pi/(5t)}$ dominates the polynomial growth $t^{-2}$, so
$$
\lim_{t\to0^+}\sqrt{5}\,t^{-2}\,e^{-2\pi/(5t)}=0.
$$

Since $t\to0^+$ is equivalent to $q=e^{-2\pi t}\to1^-$, we conclude
$$
\boxed{\displaystyle\lim_{q\to1^-}\frac{\phi^5(q)_\infty}{\phi(q^5)_\infty}=0.}
$$
